transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Reed (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions), Jane Miller (CTO - Martell Bank), Luis Ortega (Head of InfoSec), Priya Singh (Cloud Infra), Tomás Alvarez (Compliance)
---
00:00 Alex Reed: hey everyone thanks for joining, um i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick us off. how's the audio?
00:08 Jane Miller: good here, thanks alex.
00:12 Alex Reed: great, so quick agenda - encryption at rest and in transit, our KMS options (managed keys, customer-managed, HSM), audit logging and evidence for auditors, then open q&a, and next steps. samir and maya from our security/infrastructure side will go deeper.
00:30 Luis Ortega: yeah, just to be clear our primary ask is we need HSM-backed BYOK for production, and auditable key access logs. also we have to show separation of duties for the auditors.
00:44 Samir Patel: absolutely, that's a common ask; we support CMEK-type integrations and BYOK workflows. just to set expectations: you can use cloud KMS (aws/gcp/az) with HSM-backed keys or an on-prem HSM via our Private deployment.
01:03 Priya Singh: quick Q, does redwood call the KMS on every token request or is it just during key wrap/unwrap? that impacts latency.
01:11 Maya Chen: good Q. we do envelope encryption: we keep data-encryption-keys (DEKs) encrypted by your CMK. DEKs are cached at the host and we only call the KMS on key unwrap/wrap events — so per-request latency for token generation isn't calling KMS. there is a small overhead for initial setup and occasional re-wraps.
01:34 Jane Miller: can you expand on "cached at the host"? who manages the cache?
01:38 Samir Patel: the runtime holds DEKs in memory on the serving nodes; under Private or Dedicated we run in your VPC or reserved pool and the DEKs are protected in process memory. we take steps to rotate and purge caches on node restarts or redeploys.
01:56 Luis Ortega: ok but from an audit perspective we need to show access logs to the CMK — who calls it and when. are those logs accessible to us?
02:05 Maya Chen: yes, if you use your cloud KMS, the cloud provider (aws cloudtrail, gcp audit logs) records the calls. for Redwood-managed keys we provide our audit logs and can include key usage events in the console. for BYOK with customer KMS, you'll have the canonical logs.
02:24 Tomás Alvarez: auditors will want immutable logs for key admin ops and rotations. can you support WORM or long-term retention?
02:31 Alex Reed: we can export audit events to your SIEM/S3/GCS for long retention; we also support retention policies on our side for console logs but for regulatory proof we recommend pushing to customer-controlled storage.
02:45 Priya Singh: what's the HSM story if we want cloud HSM vs on-prem HSM?
02:50 Samir Patel: two paths: 1) cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS CMKs, or Google Cloud HSM) — you own the CMK in your cloud and it's HSM-backed; Redwood integrates via the cloud KMS API. 2) on-prem HSM or key broker with our Private deployment — we run the control plane in your environment and can connect to your HSM over secure channels. both support BYOK.
03:17 Jane Miller: any performance numbers when using cloud HSM CMKs? just curious about latency for key unwraps under heavy load.
03:23 Maya Chen: unwrap is a single remote call; typical KMS unwrap latencies are 20-80 ms depending on provider and region. since we cache DEKs the steady-state per-token overhead is negligible. we'll run a bench for your region and HSM config.
03:40 Luis Ortega: rotation is another area — auditors want a rotation policy. can remote rotation be forced by us?
03:46 Samir Patel: you control rotation when you own the CMK. You can rotate on a schedule and the DEK wrap will be re-encrypted on next access or via a rewrap job. Redwood can trigger rewrap jobs during maintenance windows if you want an automated process.
04:04 Jane Miller: do you support key versioning and key policy restrictions (e.g., only certain principals can use the key)?
04:11 Maya Chen: yes, key policies are managed at the KMS layer; with cloud KMS you can set IAM policies and only give access to service accounts that Redwood uses. with Private we integrate with your identity controls.
04:22 Priya Singh: how do we authenticate the Redwood agents when they call our KMS? is that mTLS or an IAM role?
04:27 Samir Patel: depends on deployment: for Hosted we use provider-level service accounts / roles for KMS. For Private/VPC we can do mTLS and client certs, or use a bastion with pre-established trust. we also support SPIFFE-style identities in some deployments.
04:48 Tomás Alvarez: registry of key admin ops — who is allowed to rotate or delete — that must be separated. can you show RBAC for that?
04:55 Alex Reed: in our Console we expose role-based controls for operational actions; for critical KMS operations we recommend doing them in the customer's KMS so the policies live there, and Redwood's role is limited to requesting wraps/unwrapps. we can show a matrix in the follow-up doc.
05:10 Jane Miller: let's go through a sample workflow — we want BYOK with an AWS CMK that is HSM-backed, plus alerts on key usage. what's the flow?
05:18 Samir Patel: step 1: create a CMK in your AWS account with CloudHSM backing (or HSM key material). step 2: grant Redwood a restricted IAM principal with kms:Encrypt kms:Decrypt and CloudTrail access. step 3: Redwood uses that CMK to wrap DEKs during startup; CloudTrail will record kms:GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls. step 4: DEKs live in runtime memory; if a node restarts we fetch and unwrap the DEK. step 5: you configure CloudTrail & CloudWatch alerts for unusual key access patterns.
06:02 Luis Ortega: if an attacker gets access to a runtime node's memory could they get the DEK? how do you mitigate that?
06:09 Maya Chen: we use standard memory protections, minimal retention windows, and we rotate DEKs frequently; nodes are ephemeral and we enforce strict host-level security. for the highest assurance you can combine with Private + HSM-based on-prem so the key material never leaves your HSM.
06:32 Priya Singh: do you support bringing HSM key material into cloud KMS (imported key) or do we need CloudHSM?
06:38 Samir Patel: you can import key material into some KMSes; AWS has imported keys and CloudHSM, GCP has externally hosted keys. the practical option for most banks is CloudHSM-backed CMKs or an on-prem HSM via Private. we'll detail pros/cons in the guide.
06:59 Jane Miller: encryption in transit — TLS 1.3 ok? mutual TLS? we have internal network constraints.
07:05 Alex Reed: we support TLS 1.3 for all in-transit. For Private deployments we can configure mTLS and client certs. For hosted API, we use TLS + OAuth/static tokens; if you require mTLS we can do that via a dedicated VPC/Private link.
07:22 Priya Singh: does Redwood support VPC endpoints or private link into the control plane?
07:27 Samir Patel: yes, Private supports VPC peering, PrivateLink, and on-prem connectors. Dedicated capacity can be placed in dedicated VPCs too.
07:39 Tomás Alvarez: about logs: can key usage events be exported as structured events with user/principal and timestamp? auditors need who/what/when.
07:48 Maya Chen: yep — cloud KMS events have the principal and request parameters; Redwood also emits structured events for model and request flows with token counts, model id, and the KMS call references. we can push all of that to your SIEM with event fields that match your schema.
08:05 Jane Miller: small thing — what about secrets management for config (like DB creds)? does Redwood integrate with vaults?
08:11 Samir Patel: we support HashiCorp Vault, cloud secret managers, and you can bring values via Private deployment connectors. Secrets used by the runtime are stored in memory and not persisted unencrypted.
08:23 Luis Ortega: one more compliance note — we need evidence for key custody during our internal audit. do you provide attestation that keys were only accessed by authorized service identities?
08:31 Maya Chen: yes, between CloudTrail logs, our audit logs, and signed receipts we can provide a chain of evidence. for highest assurance we recommend you keep CMKs in your account.
08:46 Jane Miller: what about HSM latency under burst loads? we need to understand tail latencies because our SLAs are strict.
08:53 Maya Chen: tail latencies for KMS can spike under contention; that's why caching DEKs is important. for bursty traffic we typically use a combination of cache warmers and increased DEK rotation windows during peak. we'll run a bench simulating your load.
09:12 Priya Singh: are there any crypto algorithms choices we need to enforce? like AES-GCM vs other modes?
09:17 Samir Patel: we default to AES-256-GCM for data keys and RSA/ECC only for signing operations. the KMS supports algorithm choices where applicable; we'll document exact ciphers and TLS configs.
09:29 Tomás Alvarez: regarding key compromise — what's the incident process? immediate revocation, forensic logs, notification SLA?
09:36 Alex Reed: we have an incident process and will follow the agreed SLA. if the CMK is compromised you can revoke or disable it, then rewrap DEKs with a new CMK; we'll support compromised-key rotation playbook and provide logs forensics. notification windows depend on your contract level; we'll propose 24-hour initial notification for pilot.
09:58 Jane Miller: can we get an outline of the playbook?
10:00 Alex Reed: yes we'll include a draft incident playbook in the follow-up package.
10:06 Luis Ortega: a few nitpicks: 1) multi-region key replication — do you support automatic rewrap and key replication? 2) key attestation from HSM vendor?
10:16 Maya Chen: 1) for multi-region we recommend creating CMKs in each region and use replication approaches; Redwood can orchestrate rewrap jobs across regions. 2) attestation depends on HSM vendor — CloudHSM and other providers provide attestation reports; we can store those in our docs package.
10:41 Priya Singh: about Private deployment — does the control plane need outbound internet for KMS calls?
10:47 Samir Patel: it depends. Private can be configured to call your KMS endpoints over private links or via a customer-managed egress. we can support fully air-gapped setups with on-prem HSM if you need zero outbound to public internet.
11:05 Jane Miller: auditors will ask about key lifecycle documentation, can you provide a more formal policy template?
11:10 Alex Reed: yes, we'll include sample key lifecycle and rotation policy templates.
11:15 Tomás Alvarez: curious about retention of old encrypted data when you rotate — if we rotate CMKs, do older data remain decryptable?
11:22 Maya Chen: yes, if you keep older CMK versions (key versions) you can re-decrypt old DEKs; if you destroy the old CMK material then old ciphertexts become unrecoverable. retention is a customer decision; we'll show recommended workflows.
11:38 Priya Singh: any special requirements for PCI/PII redaction during logging? we need to ensure logs don't contain sensitive snippets.
11:44 Samir Patel: Redwood supports configurable log scrubbing and we can redact prompt/user content before exporting. we recommend exporting metadata only for audit trails with request ids rather than raw content for regulated data.
12:02 Jane Miller: ok let's talk about concrete pilot - we want to try HSM-backed AWS CMK in us-east-1 with a small dedicated pool. what do you need from us?
12:12 Alex Reed: we'll need an IAM principal to grant kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt, CloudTrail enabled, sample workload or traffic replay, and a contact for infra (Priya). Samir will run bench and Maya will collect logs and format them for your auditors.
12:35 Priya Singh: timeline? we want to get this into a pilot within two weeks if possible.
12:40 Alex Reed: we can target a pilot kickoff next wednesday (2026-10-28) pending access. Samir: is that doable?
12:45 Samir Patel: yes, we can. we'll need the IAM roles and a brief infra checklist — i'll send that today.
12:52 Luis Ortega: last question, SSO/RBAC: will redwood's operators ever be able to trigger key rotations in our KMS?
12:59 Maya Chen: not unless you grant that permission. our recommended pattern is to keep rotation controls in your KMS and only give Redwood limited encrypt/decrypt rights. we'll document a least-privilege IAM policy.
13:18 Jane Miller: excellent, that covers my main concerns. can you also provide the SOC 2 attestation and iso docs?
13:24 Alex Reed: yes, i'll put those in the follow-up email with the KMS guide and proposed SOW.
13:30 Tomás Alvarez: thanks all, expect questions from auditors; we'll route them through tomás and priya.
13:35 Alex Reed: great. quick recap then next steps and action owners — we'll send notes. thanks everyone.
---
End of meeting
